verses.text: When the LORD was about to take Elijah up to heaven in a whirlwind, Elijah and Elisha were leaving Gilgal.

Elijah said to Elisha, "Please stay here, because the LORD has sent me to Bethel." But Elisha said, "As surely as the LORD lives and as you live, I will not leave you." So they went down to Bethel together.
The group of prophets at Bethel came out to Elisha and asked, "Do you know that the LORD is going to take your master from you today?" Elisha said, "Yes, I know. Do not talk about it."

Then Elijah said to him, "Elisha, please stay here, because the LORD has sent me to Jericho." But Elisha said, "As surely as the LORD lives and as you live, I will not leave you." So they went to Jericho.
The group of prophets at Jericho came to Elisha and asked, "Do you know that the LORD is going to take your master from you today?" He answered, "Yes, I know. Do not talk about it."

Then Elijah said to him, "Please stay here, because the LORD has sent me to the Jordan River." But Elisha said, "As surely as the LORD lives and as you live, I will not leave you." So the two of them walked on.
Fifty men from the group of prophets went and stood at a distance, facing them, while Elijah and Elisha stood by the Jordan.
Elijah took off his cloak, rolled it up, and struck the water with it. The water split to the right and to the left, and the two of them crossed over on dry ground.
When they had crossed, Elijah said to Elisha, "Tell me, what can I do for you before I am taken away from you?" Elisha answered, "Please let me receive a double share of your spirit."
Elijah said, "You have asked for something hard. But if you see me when I am taken from you, you will have it. If you do not see me, you will not."
As they were walking along and talking, suddenly a chariot of fire and horses of fire came between them. And Elijah went up to heaven in a whirlwind.
Elisha saw it and cried out, "My father! My father! The chariots and horsemen of Israel!" Then he could not see him anymore. Elisha took hold of his own clothes and tore them in two.
He picked up the cloak that had fallen from Elijah, went back, and stood on the bank of the Jordan.

He took the cloak that had fallen from Elijah and struck the water with it. He said, "Where is the LORD, the God of Elijah?" When he struck the water, it split to the right and to the left, and Elisha crossed over.
The group of prophets from Jericho, who were watching, saw him and said, "The spirit of Elijah is now on Elisha." They came to meet him and bowed down to the ground in front of him.

They said, "Look, we your servants have fifty strong men with us. Please let them go and look for your master. Maybe the LORD's Spirit has picked him up and set him down on some mountain or in some valley." Elisha said, "No, do not send them."
But they kept pressing him until he was too embarrassed to refuse. So he said, "Send them." They sent fifty men, who searched for three days but did not find Elijah.
When they came back to Elisha, who was staying in Jericho, he said to them, "Didn't I tell you not to go?"
The men of Jericho said to Elisha, "Look, master, this town is in a good place, as you can see. But the water is bad, and the land does not produce crops."
Elisha said, "Bring me a new bowl and put salt in it." So they brought it to him.
He went out to the spring and threw the salt into it. He said, "This is what the LORD says: 'I have healed this water. It will never again cause death or make the land unable to produce.'"
And the water has stayed healed to this day, just as Elisha said.
From there Elisha went up to Bethel. As he was walking along the road, some young men came out of the town and made fun of him. They said, "Go on up, baldy! Go on up, baldy!"
He turned around, looked at them, and cursed them in the LORD's name. Then two female bears came out of the woods and tore forty-two of the young men to pieces.
Elisha went on from there to Mount Carmel, and from there he went back to Samaria.
